Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Planner Agent
You are a professor responsible for planning deep and effective research strategies to improve the **diagnosis tools for a recommender system** (diagnosis_tools.py).

You will be provided with the context of:
 - a research problem based on an initial research question
 - a starting research idea, possibly with a history showing how idea evolves through previous attempt
 - inspirations from earlier attempts
 - Users' current qualitative feedbacks
 - The analysis report on models and diagnosis tool
 - The current model and diagnosis tool design and code analysis, including how personas, traits, and feedback JSON are defined

Your task is to develop search queries that guide researchers toward **substantial improvements to the diagnosis toolkit**, not just minor metric tweaks. Focus on directions such as:
    - New probes/metrics that better capture real failure modes
    - New probes/metrics that capture user's feedbacks
    - Better ways to connect probes to specific model components and training signals
    - Methods to validate, stress-test, or calibrate these metrics so they are trustworthyRather than combining existing inspirations in small increments, the queries should guide researchers toward substantial evolutions. 
Because other researchers will rely on this plan, it must emphasize major, novel approaches instead of minor refinements.

You will also be told whether the research progress is early or mature:
- If the progress is early, focus on ideas that are feasible and practical, and can grow later and have great future potential.
- If the progress is mature, focus on bold, high-impact shifts that challenge the current approach.

Your plan should follow two steps:
1. Formulate 1 to 3 precise and diverse search queries. Make sure the queries are diverse—cover different perspectives, challenge untested assumptions, and explore alternative methods. 
2. For each query, include a short note explaining why you chose it and what you hope it will reveal.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe accesses the trained `nn.Module` through a compatibility adapter; model architecture is not shown. `view.log2feats(sequence)` produces B × L × D features. The final user representation is `features[:, -1, :]`, computed from the latest L interactions, left-padded with zeros. `view.predict_score` converts features and item IDs into logits; `view.item_emb` supplies catalog embeddings.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` snapshots `view.user_train` histories and optional timestamps. It never consumes `train_loader`; training-margin batches are generated independently. Optional dataset routing and five supplied user IDs identify the exploratory panel. Missing panels are reported without sampling replacements.

Diagnosis runs in evaluation and inference modes, restoring module flags and Python, NumPy, and torch RNG states afterward.

# Probes & Metrics

- **History sensitivity:** Measures top-10 overlap, displacement of original top-10 items in full-catalog ranks, strict pair-order reversals, mean absolute logit change, and final-feature L2 change. Higher overlap and smaller changes indicate stability, not accuracy.
- **Training margins:** Samples 320 eligible-user draws with replacement and teacher-forced transitions, using uniform negatives outside each user’s complete training history. Reports mean margin, empirical p10, negative-beats-positive rate, and margin-below-0.5 rate. Larger margins suggest better sampled training separation, subject to logit scale.
- **Embedding geometry:** Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding embeddings. Reports mean cosine, normalized effective rank from centered singular values, leading singular-value mass, norms, and zero counts. Strong alignment or concentrated spectra can flag restricted geometry but do not establish collapse.

# Perturbation & Tests

Edits include identity, recent/old deletion, last-item-only, anchor-preserving deletion, random deletion, full shuffle, and prefix shuffle. Stochastic edits use five seeded draws. Each user retains the same full-catalog candidate pool excluding their complete original history.

Matched contrasts compare deletion location and final-item preservation. Edits compact positions, so content and positional effects are intertwined. Identity, repeated-inference, and positive-rescaling checks audit consistency.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

The returned object contains `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Metrics include panel metadata, baseline audits, edit aggregates, paired contrasts, per-draw records, margins, geometry, failures/counts, provenance hashes, integrity checks, and diagnostic cost. Full rank arrays remain in `rank_cache`.

Aggregates weight users equally and include exploratory bootstrap intervals. Five-user panels are not representative. No validation accuracy, semantic sensitivity, simulator traits, or causal improvement is established. Four-category aggregation is external; host macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection metric.
